    {
      "modified": "2026-06-25T06:28:32Z",
      "published": "2026-06-25T05:29:26Z",
      "schema_version": "1.7.4",
      "id": "MAL-2026-6440",
      "summary": "Malicious code in tokenization-util (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (81f8a194aa79844110dede95f5f8c798d05c04c08f1a4f5d8822124b17c65fa6)\nThe package advertises plain math/formatter helpers but index.js contains a heavily obfuscated payload concealed inside the calculateTokenPrice function. The payload is hidden behind ~1500 leading tab characters of visual padding, then uses two seeded Fisher-Yates string-shuffler decoders and String.fromCharCode splicing to reconstruct the identifiers 'constructor', 'require', and 'module' at runtime. The code resolves Function via yLb[kqz] (a string-shuffled property lookup for 'constructor'), uses that Function constructor to build a decoder from one shuffled blob, decodes a second scrambled blob into JS source, and invokes that source via Function(...)(3004). It also assigns the CommonJS require and module bindings to globalThis (global[require]=require; global[module]=module), giving the decoded code access to any Node built-in (network, fs, child_process) regardless of how the package is imported. None of this behavior is documented in the README or exposed through the advertised API. The combination of multi-layer obfuscation, visual concealment via tab padding, dynamic eval of decoded literals, and forced global exposure of require/module is the canonical shape of a hidden remote-code-execution backdoor in an npm utility package \u2014 the decoded payload runs whenever calculateTokenPrice is called by a consumer.\n",

    {
      "modified": "2026-06-25T06:28:31Z",
      "published": "2026-06-25T05:56:41Z",
      "schema_version": "1.7.4",
      "id": "MAL-2026-6438",
      "summary": "Malicious code in polymarket-stake-math (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (a8a5200cef3811ce98e489080709917dfafc2216a17f90329b9930e0f5f630a1)\nThe package ships a `postinstall` hook (`scripts/sync-peer.cjs`) that runs on every default `npm install`. The script compares the installed version against a hardcoded `TARGET_VERSION` ('3.4.0'); because the shipped version is 3.5.0, the mismatch branch always fires. It then invokes `execSync('npm pack polymarket-stake-math@3.4.0'...)`, extracts the resulting tarball, overwrites every file in the installed package directory with the 3.4.0 contents via `fs.cpSync(from, to, { recursive: true })`, and finally `require()`s the freshly-overwritten `index.js` and calls `from_str()`. This is a stager pattern: the published 3.5.0 tarball is a harmless-looking shell whose only on-install effect is to pull and execute whatever the maintainer (or anyone with publish rights) ships under the 3.4.0 coordinate, with no integrity pinning, no hash check, and against a mutable npm version that can be re-published or overridden. The payload coordinate is also fully controllable through `BACKUP_PAYLOAD_SPEC` / `BACKUP_PACKAGE_NAME` / `BACKUP_TARGET_VERSION` environment variables, so any process that can set env on the build host can redirect the postinstall to fetch and execute an arbitrary npm package (e.g. `BACKUP_PAYLOAD_SPEC=evilpkg@1.0.0`). The cover-story filename 'sync-peer.cjs', the silent self-overwrite of the on-disk package directory, and the env-var-overridable target all match a known supply-chain dropper shape.\n",

      },
      "containers": {
        "cna": {
          "title": "Kernel: ksmbd brute force delay bypass via asynchronous requests",
          "metrics": [
            {
              "other": {
                "content": {
                  "value": "Low",
                  "namespace": "https://access.redhat.com/security/updates/classification/"
                },
                "type": "Red Hat severity rating"
              }
            },
            {
              "cvssV3_1": {
                "attackComplexity": "HIGH",
                "attackVector": "NETWORK",
                "availabilityImpact": "NONE",
                "baseScore": 3.7,
                "baseSeverity": "LOW",
                "confidentialityImpact": "LOW",
                "integrityImpact": "NONE",
                "privilegesRequired": "NONE",
                "scope": "UNCHANGED",
                "userInteraction": "NONE",
                "vectorString": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N",
                "version": "3.1"
              },
              "format": "CVSS"
            }
          ],
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "A vulnerability has been identified in the Linux kernel's ksmbd component (kernel SMB/CIFS server). A security control designed to prevent dictionary attacks, which introduces a 5-second delay during session setup, can be bypassed through the use of asynchronous requests. This bypass negates the intended anti-brute-force protection, potentially allowing attackers to conduct dictionary attacks more efficiently against user credentials or other authentication mechanisms."
            }
          ],
          "affected": [
            {
              "versions": [
                {

          "metrics": [
            {
              "other": {

              "format": "CVSS"
            }
          ],
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "A flaw was found in libssh. This vulnerability allows local man-in-the-middle attacks, security downgrades of SSH (Secure Shell) connections, and manipulation of trusted host information, posing a significant risk to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of SSH communications via an insecure default configuration on Windows systems where the library automatically loads configuration files from the C:\\etc directory, which can be created and modified by unprivileged local users."
            }
          ],

      "containers": {
        "cna": {
          "title": "Libxslt: type confusion in exsltfuncresultcompfunction of libxslt",
          "metrics": [
            {
              "other": {
                "content": {
                  "value": "Low",
                  "namespace": "https://access.redhat.com/security/updates/classification/"
                },
                "type": "Red Hat severity rating"
              }
            },
            {
              "cvssV3_1": {
                "attackComplexity": "HIGH",
                "attackVector": "NETWORK",
                "availabilityImpact": "LOW",
                "baseScore": 3.1,
                "baseSeverity": "LOW",
                "confidentialityImpact": "NONE",
                "integrityImpact": "NONE",

                "scope": "UNCHANGED",
                "userInteraction": "REQUIRED",
                "vectorString": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L",
                "version": "3.1"
              },
              "format": "CVSS"
            }
          ],
          "descriptions": [
            {
              "lang": "en",
              "value": "A flaw was found in the exsltFuncResultComp() function of libxslt, which handles EXSLT  elements during stylesheet parsing. Due to improper type handling, the function may treat an XML document node as a regular XML element node, resulting in a type confusion. This can cause unexpected memory reads and potential crashes. While difficult to exploit, the flaw could lead to application instability or denial of service."
            }
          ],

    {
      "modified": "2026-06-25T06:14:06Z",
      "published": "2026-06-25T06:14:06Z",
      "schema_version": "1.7.4",
      "id": "MAL-2026-6437",
      "summary": "Malicious code in logfmt-core (npm)",
      "details": "\n---\n_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_\n\n## Source: amazon-inspector (bb22b2557674e7d616805d8a4086d69e02896be169b9e5d4d053eb3628ebe038)\nOn npm install, scripts/install-check.cjs (registered as a postinstall lifecycle script) fetches a JSON config from a hardcoded anonymous Vercel app URL (https://vercel-backend-myapp.vercel.app/config/logfmt-sync.json), parses it to obtain a.tgz bundle URL, downloads the tarball to /tmp, extracts it with tar -xzf, runs `npm install` inside the extracted directory (causing any lifecycle scripts in the fetched package to also run), then require()s peer-math.js from the bundle and invokes syncSession(). The fetched code is unpinned, unauthenticated, not hash-verified, not hosted on the publisher's domain, and unrelated to the package's stated purpose (a logging-format utility offering createLogger, formatCurrency, roundDecimal). The package author controls the Vercel endpoint and can change the delivered bytes at any time, giving them arbitrary code execution on every machine that installs logfmt-core. Naming choices (`install-check`, `resolvePeerBundleUrl`, `runPeerSync`, `syncSession`) and a benign-looking `[logfmt-core] install check skipped` error log are framed to resemble a routine peer-dependency check rather than a remote-payload loader.\n",
      "affected": [
        {
          "package": {
            "ecosystem": "npm",
            "name": "logfmt-core"
          },
          "versions": [
            "3.5.2"
          ],
          "database_specific": {
            "cwes": [
              {
                "cweId": "CWE-506",
                "description": "The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.",
                "name": "Embedded Malicious Code"
              }
            ],
            "indicators": {
              "evidence_files": [
                {
                  "path": "scripts/install-check.cjs",
                  "sha256": "aebcb6ffec4c38aa0374f6cf844c69c933153c0c42a71f80190086a230b5de01",
                  "tlsh": "f9a1659519a6727346b1ebb8c722901eef2390232511c360f6de96912fb72a4c352dec"
                }
              ],
              "package_integrity": [
                {
                  "filename": "logfmt-core-3.5.2.tgz",
                  "hashes": {
                    "sha1": "fee2963003b831b562f802872c51ed180f8a9023",
                    "sha512_sri": "sha512-7IjRE0IZONd6vHfd4hiyT5OJBUV1uKcLVsgvELO/BojZ+2QaLV+21eiuD3GdBclxJ9JLJVFnQRzYOkz/94LVvg=="
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }

            "headline": "Marine Weather Statement issued June 25 at 1:56AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "The areas affected include...\nCoastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island\nLouisiana out 20 to 60 NM...\nCoastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20\nNM...\n\nAt 155 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of strong\nthunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This\ncluster of thunderstorms is generally located along a line extending\nfrom 6 nm southwest of Petit Bois Pass to 27 nm southeast of\nChandeleur Sound, moving southeast at 15 knots.",
            "instruction": "Mariners can expect widespread gusty winds to around 30 knots, higher\nwaves, and dangerous lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe\nharbor immediately until this activity passes.\n\nThis cluster of strong thunderstorms will likely produce winds to\naround 30 knots, and could pose a serious hazard for boaters.             "description": "...WARM, WINDY AND DRY THURSDAY...\n\n* Affected Area: Colville Reservation (Zone 702), Okanogan Valley\n(Zone 703), Foothills of Central Washington Cascades (Zone 705),\nWaterville Plateau (Zone 706), Western Columbia Basin (Zone\n707), Eastern Columbia Basin -Palouse -Spokane Area (Zone 708)\nand Lower Palouse-Snake River (Zone 709).\n\n* Winds: Southwest 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* Relative Humidities: 12 to 21 percent.\n\n* Impacts: Rapid fire spread is likely with any new or ongoing\nfires.",

            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 1:42AM CDT until June 25 at 6:33PM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Wichita KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nChikaskia River near Corbin affecting Sumner County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.\n\n* WHERE...Chikaskia River near Corbin.\n\n* WHEN...From early this morning to this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Flooding of low-lying areas can be\nexpected, especially along the right bank.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1:16 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 11.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.6\nfeet early this morning. It will then fall below flood stage\nlate this morning.\n- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this afternoon at 145 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 1:40AM CDT until June 25 at 5:30AM CDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "FFWGLD\n\nThe National Weather Service in Goodland has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nNorthern Decatur County in northwestern Kansas...\nSouthern Red Willow County in southwestern Nebraska...\n\n* Until 530 AM CDT.\n\n* At 140 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain\nhave fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible\nin the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nMcCook, Oberlin, Norcatur, Danbury, Lebanon, Cedar Bluffs and\nTraer.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "senderName": "NWS Paducah KY",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:36AM CDT until June 27 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southern Illinois, including the following\nareas, Alexander, Edwards, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin,\nJackson, Jefferson, Johnson, Massac, Perry IL, Pope, Pulaski,\nSaline, Union, Wabash, Wayne IL, White and Williamson, southwest\nIndiana, including the following areas, Gibson, Pike, Posey,\nSpencer, Vanderburgh and Warrick, western Kentucky, including the\nfollowing areas, Henderson and Union KY, and southeast Missouri,\nincluding the following areas, Bollinger, Butler, Cape Girardeau,\nCarter, Perry MO, Ripley, Scott, Stoddard and Wayne MO.\n\n* WHEN...From this afternoon through Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple rounds of thunderstorms are expected through Friday\nnight. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall from thunderstorms\ncould produce flash flooding.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:32AM CDT until June 25 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, southwest, and western Arkansas,\nincluding the following areas, in central Arkansas, Garland. In\nsouthwest Arkansas, Clark, Hot Spring and Pike. In western\nArkansas, Central and Eastern Montgomery County, Central and\nSouthern Scott County, Northern Montgomery County Higher\nElevations, Northern Polk County Higher Elevations, Northern Scott\nCounty, Polk County Lower Elevations, Southeast Polk County Higher\nElevations and Southwest Montgomery County Higher Elevations.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1 PM CDT this afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- The flood watch is conditional on the basis that showers and\nthunderstorms develop during the morning hours on Thursday.\nIf this scenario pans out, amounts between one and three\ninches will be possible over portions of western to southwest\nArkansas and much of the Ouachita Mountains. In addition to\nforecast rainfall, much of the area received one to two\ninches of rainfall Wednesday afternoon, resulting in primed\nsoils for runoff and flash flooding.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:23AM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southeast Kansas, including the following\nareas, Bourbon, Cherokee and Crawford and Missouri, including the\nfollowing areas, Barton, Benton, Camden, Cedar, Dade, Dallas,\nDent, Greene, Hickory, Jasper, Laclede, Lawrence, Maries, Miller,\nMorgan, Phelps, Polk, Pulaski, St. Clair, Texas, Vernon, Webster\nand Wright.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 PM CDT this afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Bands of heavy rainfall with amounts around 2 to 4 inches\nexpected, with localized higher amounts up to 6 inches.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 12:20AM MDT until June 27 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "description": "...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM LATE SATURDAY MORNING THROUGH\nSATURDAY EVENING DUE TO STRONG WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR\nMUCH OF NORTHWEST AND NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO AS WELL AS THE CENTRAL\nHIGHLANDS...\n\n.Critical fire weather conditions will return on Saturday across much\nof northwest and northeast New Mexico as well as the Central\nHighlands. Strong southwest winds with gusts up to 45 mph and\nhumidity values falling below 15 percent are expected. This will come\nafter several days with thunderstorms with spotty rainfall. Any\nlightning-started fires will have the potential to grow quickly under\nthese fire weather conditions.\n\nThe National Weather Service in Albuquerque NM has issued a Fire\nWeather Watch.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Northwest Plateau (Zone 101), Northeast Plains\n(Zone 104), West Central Mountains (Zone 105), North Central\nMountains (Zone 120), Upper Rio Grande Valley and Lower Chama River\nValley (Zone 121), Northeast Highlands (Zone 123), and Central\nHighlands (Zone 125).\n\n* TIMING...From Saturday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* 20 FOOT WINDS...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45\nmph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative humidity between 10 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor\nburning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of\nthis Fire Weather Watch.",

            "senderName": "NWS Amarillo TX",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 1:18AM CDT until June 25 at 4:30AM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "FFWAMA\n\nThe National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSouth Central Potter County in the panhandle of Texas...\nNorth Central Randall County in the panhandle of Texas...\n\n* Until 430 AM CDT.\n\n* At 118 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Up to 2 inches of rain have\nfallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nAmarillo.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "event": "Fire Weather Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Denver CO",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 12:18AM MDT until June 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "...PROLONGED CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED FOR THE\nHIGH COUNTRY...\n\nA warm and dry airmass will coincide with considerably stronger\nwest and southwest winds this weekend, potentially continuing into\nearly next week. Sustained winds are expected to exceed 20 to 30\nmph across much of the high country beginning Saturday, with gusts\nof 40 to 50 mph, strongest for exposed areas and higher\nelevations. These conditions will drive very high fire danger\nacross the warned area, that may extend through the evening hours\nof Saturday driven by the enhanced winds. Any new starts or\nestablished fires will likely spread rapidly under these\nconditions.\n\nThe National Weather Service in Denver has issued a Fire Weather\nWatch for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect from\nSaturday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 211, 212, 213, 214, 217 and\n218.\n\n* TIMING...From Saturday morning through late Saturday evening.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 20 to 25 mph with gusts 40 to 50 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...11 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Conditions will be favorable for rapid fire spread.\nAvoid outdoor burning and any activity that may produce a\nspark and start a wildfire.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "RFWBOU"
              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [
                "WWUS85 KBOU 250618"
              ],

            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas, Pike\nIL and Randolph IL and Missouri, including the following areas,\nAudrain MO, Iron MO, Madison MO, Pike MO, Reynolds MO, Saint\nFrancois MO and Sainte Genevieve MO.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 PM CDT this afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple waves of thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall.\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nFarmington, Mexico, Chester, Bonne Terre, Bowling Green, Desloge,\nPittsfield, Ste.             "senderName": "NWS St Louis MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:16AM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas, Bond\nIL, Calhoun IL, Clinton IL, Fayette IL, Greene IL, Jersey IL,\nMacoupin IL, Madison IL, Marion IL, Monroe IL, Montgomery IL, Saint\nClair IL and Washington IL and Missouri, including the following\nareas, Boone MO, Callaway MO, Cole MO, Crawford MO, Franklin MO,\nGasconade MO, Jefferson MO, Lincoln MO, Moniteau MO, Montgomery MO,\nOsage MO, Saint Charles MO, Saint Louis City MO, Saint Louis MO,\nWarren MO and Washington MO.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 PM CDT this afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple waves of thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall.\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nSt. Louis, Columbia, O'Fallon, St. Charles, St. Peters,\nFlorissant, Chesterfield, Belleville, Jefferson City, Wildwood,\nUniversity City, Ballwin, Granite City, Wentzville, Alton,\nKirkwood, Maryland Heights, East St. Louis and Hazelwood.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:16AM CDT until June 27 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "Wet antecedent conditions from recent active weather means that it\nwill not take much additional rainfall for flooding to occur,\nespecially in low lying areas.  Current forecast guidance exhibits a\nhigh (greater than 70%) probability of exceeding 2 inches of\nrainfall within the watch area.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and southeast Illinois,\nincluding the following counties, in central Illinois, Christian\nand Shelby. In east central Illinois, Clark, Coles, Cumberland and\nMoultrie. In southeast Illinois, Clay, Crawford, Effingham,\nJasper, Lawrence and Richland.\n\n* WHEN...From this afternoon through Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 12:10AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 12:11AM MDT until June 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Fire Weather\nWatch for gusty winds and low relative humidity, which is in\neffect from Saturday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 220, 222, 223, 224 and 225.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 10 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Elevated fire danger is expected.             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 12:10AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 10:58PM PDT until June 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR",
            "description": "...Breezy winds and low relative humidity expected Thursday...\n\n.The combination of breezy winds and low relative humidity is\nexpected to generate weather conditions conducive to rapid fire\nspread for new and existing fires in the lower Columbia Basin,\nYakima and Kittitas valleys, and the Warm Springs Reservation.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 690 Kittitas Valley and 691\nLower Columbia Basin of Washington.\n\n* TIMING...From noon to 9 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* WINDS...West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 10 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread\nquickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Midland/Odessa TX",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 25 at 12:50AM CDT until June 25 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX",
            "description": "* WHAT...Temperatures up to 113 expected.\n\n* WHERE...Lower Brewster County, Presidio Valley, and Rio Grande\nValley.\n\n* WHEN...From 2 PM this afternoon to 9 PM CDT this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses. Extreme heat\nwill significantly increase the potential for heat related\nillnesses, particularly for those working or participating in\noutdoor activities.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids even if you don't feel thirsty, but avoid\nalcohol and caffeine. Stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on elderly and vulnerable relatives and\nneighbors.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nLook before you lock! Do not leave young children and pets in\nunattended vehicles for even a moment. Car interiors will very\nquickly reach lethal temperatures.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "description": "* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive\nrainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...East Central Fremont County in central Wyoming...\n\n* WHEN...Until 200 AM MDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\nWater over roadways.             "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.             "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 11:30PM CDT until June 25 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Arkansas, including the following counties,\nColumbia, Hempstead, Howard, Lafayette, Little River, Miller,\nNevada, Sevier and Union, Louisiana, including the following\nparishes, Bienville, Claiborne, Jackson, Lincoln, Ouachita, Union\nand Webster, southeast Oklahoma, including the following county,\nMcCurtain, and northeast Texas, including the following county,\nBowie.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional showers and thunderstorms are expected to redevelop\nduring the overnight and towards Thursday morning. With extremely\nsaturated soils from heavy rainfall that has fallen over the last\nseveral days, it wont take much rain to cause Flash Flooding\nconcerns. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches, with\nisolated higher amounts, are possible across much of the Watch\narea.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Chicago IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:56PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Chicago IL has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Indiana...Illinois...\n\nLittle Calumet River at Munster (Hohman Avenue) affecting Cook\nand Lake IN Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Near flood stage water levels likely.\n\n* WHERE...Little Calumet River from IN-912 in Hammond downstream to\nconfluence with Thorn Creek in South Holland, including the\nMunster (Hohman Avenue) gauge.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Water overflows low-lying river banks\noutside of the levee-protected area in Hammond and Munster.\nAt 12.5 feet, Most areas outside of the levee-protected area are\ninundated in Hammond and Munster.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 11.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to near flood stage\novernight tonight.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or\nmay already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the\nwarned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and\nproperty.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by Thursday afternoon.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Amarillo TX",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 10:53PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Beaver County in the Oklahoma Panhandle, and Lipscomb\nCounty in the Texas Panhandle.\n\n* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nArea creeks and streams are running high and could flood with more\nheavy rain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Recent rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches may lead to\nexcessive runoff with expected thunderstorms tonight through\ntomorrow night.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Chicago IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:43PM CDT until June 25 at 4:30AM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Southern Cook County in northeast Illinois, northern Lake\nCounty and west central Porter County in northwest Indiana.\n\n* WHEN...Until 430 AM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding\nmay occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Roads and streets may\nbe flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1040 PM CDT, stream gauge reports indicated rapid rises on\narea creeks due to earlier heavy rainfall. Multiple reports\nof roadway flooding have been received from southern Cook\nCounty into northern Lake County. Standing water on area\nroadways may be slow to recede into the overnight hours, and\nsome creeks may continue to rise overnight.\n- Some locations that may continue to experience flooding\ninclude...\nChicago, Hammond, Gary, Orland Park, Oak Lawn, Calumet City,\nMerrillville, Valparaiso, Chicago Heights, Schererville,\nHobart, Lansing, Oak Forest, Crown Point, Harvey, Highland,\nBlue Island, Munster, Dolton and Homewood. This includes\nThorn Creek, Hart Ditch, Turkey Creek, Deep River, and the\nLittle Calumet River.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Warning means flooding is imminent or may already be\noccurring. Persons along rivers, creeks, and other waterways should\ntake immediate precautions to protect life and property.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 9:26PM MDT until June 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "* AFFECTED AREA...In Colorado, Fire Weather Zone 200 Little\nSnake Forecast Area, Fire Weather Zone 202 White River\nForecast Area, Fire Weather Zone 207 Southwest Colorado Lower\nForecast Area and Fire Weather Zone 290 Paradox Valley\nForecast Area.\n\n* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, from noon to 9 PM MDT\nFriday. For the Fire Weather Watch, from Saturday morning\nthrough Saturday evening.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...9 to 14 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Elevated fire danger is expected. Fires will catch\nand spread rapidly and erratically.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.\n\nA Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",

            "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:14PM CDT until June 25 at 10:40AM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nPolecat Creek near Sapulpa affecting Creek County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Polecat Creek near Sapulpa.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, widespread flooding affects pasturelands\nand oil fields between Sapulpa and the Tulsa County line. Barns\nand other outbuildings may be threatened by minor flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:03 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 24.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is near crest and is expected to fall\nbelow flood stage late tonight and continue falling and\nremain below flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 21.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 8:10PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 106 to\n112 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...The lower Colorado River Valley, including the city of\nYuma.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat\nexhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat\nstroke.",
            "instruction": "An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

              ],

            "event": "Extreme Heat Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 8:10PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 107 to\n114 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...Western Imperial County including the city of El Centro.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat\nexhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat\nstroke.",
            "instruction": "An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [

              ],

            "event": "Extreme Heat Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 8:10PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 107 to\n113 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...The entire Phoenix metropolitan area.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat\nexhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat\nstroke.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free\ncooling center, transportation, water, and more.\nhttp://www.maricopa.gov/heat",
            "instruction": "An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Shreveport LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:04PM CDT until June 27 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nBayou D'arbonne At Lake Claiborne affecting Claiborne Parish.\n\nFor the Bayou D'arbonne...including Lake Claiborne, Lake D'Arbonne...\nModerate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou D'arbonne at Lake Claiborne.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday morning.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 188.9 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:00 PM CDT Wednesday was 188.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 189.0 feet\ntomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 188.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 189.1\nfeet on 04/14/2019.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday evening at 1015 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:03PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Arkansas...\n\nBayou Dorcheat Near Springhill affecting Webster and Columbia\nParishes.\n\nFor the Bayou Dorcheat...including Springhill, Dixie Inn, Lake\nBistineau...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou Dorcheat near Springhill.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding of private boat\nramps. Move livestock to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 13.4 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:00 PM CDT Wednesday was 13.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.0 feet\nFriday evening.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.0\nfeet on 04/01/2018.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads.             "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 9:37PM CDT until June 25 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Tulsa has issued a Flood Advisory\nfor the following rivers in Oklahoma...\n\nArkansas River near Muskogee affecting Muskogee County.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Arkansas River near Muskogee.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to tomorrow evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 27.0 feet, no flooding occurs but low lying\nagricultural areas may be threatened. Continue to monitor later\nforecasts.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 27.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.3\nfeet tomorrow morning and then slowly fall to below 27.0 feet\ntomorrow afternoon.\n- Action stage is 27.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 9:22PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of east central, northeast, and southeast\nOklahoma, including the following counties, in east central\nOklahoma, Central and Southern Sequoyah, Cherokee, Muskogee,\nNorthern Sequoyah and Okfuskee. In northeast Oklahoma, Adair,\nCraig, Creek, Delaware, Mayes, Northeast Osage, Nowata, Okmulgee,\nOttawa, Pawnee, Rogers, Southeast Osage, Tulsa, Wagoner,\nWashington OK and Western Osage. In southeast Oklahoma, Central Le\nFlore, Haskell, Latimer, McIntosh, Northern Le Flore, Pittsburg\nand Southern Le Flore.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional widespread thunderstorm development is probable\novernight\nWednesday night and through the daytime Thursday. Heavy\nrainfall\nrates of one to two inches per hour are likely, leading to\nmore\nflooding potential.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:11PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the Illinois river at the\nfollowing locations...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at La Grange LD.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 25.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will rise to 26.1 feet early Sunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the Illinois river at the\nfollowing locations...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Meredosia.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Beach Road just north of Shady Acres floods\nnear this height.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will rise to 20.3 feet early Sunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:57PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Marshall and Putnam Counties.\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Tazewell, Woodford and Peoria\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Brown, Cass, Morgan and\nSchuyler Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Cass, Fulton and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Peoria.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.6 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 20.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.7\nfeet just after midnight tonight.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:57PM CDT until June 28 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Marshall and Putnam Counties.\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Tazewell, Woodford and Peoria\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Brown, Cass, Morgan and\nSchuyler Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Cass, Fulton and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Henry.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Water begins to affect the marina in Henry\nalong with minor flooding of land adjacent to the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 24.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 24.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly Sunday afternoon and continue falling to 21.5 feet\nWednesday, July 01.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:57PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Marshall and Putnam Counties.\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Tazewell, Woodford and Peoria\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Brown, Cass, Morgan and\nSchuyler Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Cass, Fulton and Mason\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River near Havana.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, Access road to Anderson Lake north\ncampground closed.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 19.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 18.4 feet\nWednesday, July 01.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:55PM EDT until June 25 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tomorrow evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Considerable agricultural flooding extends\nfrom just north of the junction of Illinois 33 with Business 50 to\nthe St. Francesville, Illinois area.  River Road from Lincoln\nMemorial Bridge to Billett Rd is impassable.  Extensive seep water\nforms behind Illinois levees extending from Russellville to U.S.\nHighway 50.  Flooding of agricultural land begins in Knox County\nIndiana west of the railroad extending for the Oaktown area to the\nnorth side of Vincennes.  Extensive flooding of Small Creek.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:45 PM EDT Wednesday /8:45 PM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 16.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 9:45 PM EDT Wednesday /8:45 PM CDT Wednesday/ was\n16.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nlate tomorrow morning and continue falling and remain below\nflood stage.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued Thursday afternoon by around 100\nPM EDT /noon CDT/.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:55PM EDT until June 26 at 12:30AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Old Darwin Road and a few low rural roads\nbetween York and Hutsonville, Illinois begin to flood.\nAgricultural flooding begins along portions of the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- There is no current observed data.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon and continue falling and remain\nbelow flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued Thursday afternoon by around 100\nPM EDT /noon CDT/.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:55PM EDT until June 27 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All\noil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on\nsubstructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural\nlosses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher\nground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year\nround.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday /7:45 PM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 19.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:45 PM EDT Wednesday /7:45 PM CDT Wednesday/ was\n19.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will rise to 20.1 feet early tomorrow\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday\nmorning to 17.9 feet Saturday evening. It will rise to 18.1\nfeet Sunday evening. It will then fall again and remain below\nflood stage.\n- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued Thursday afternoon by around 100\nPM EDT /noon CDT/.",

            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:55PM EDT until June 25 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...White River at Petersburg.\n\n* WHEN...Until tomorrow afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Flooding affects low agricultural lands,\nlow oil fields and closes Bottoms Rd...Brothers Rd and East\nGovernors Road in Knox County.  In agricultural season...farmers\nare concerned at this stage.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 PM EDT Wednesday /8:30 PM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 17.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 9:30 PM EDT Wednesday /8:30 PM CDT Wednesday/ was\n18.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nlate tonight and continue falling and remain below flood\nstage.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued Thursday afternoon by around 100\nPM EDT /noon CDT/.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:55PM EDT until June 26 at 1:00AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the White River from Petersburg\ndown to the Wabash and on the Wabash River from the Hutsonville\narea down to Mount Carmel. The crest on the White was near Hazleton\nwhile the crest on the Wabash was near Vincennes late Wednesday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Some agricultural lands underwater.  A few\nrural roads in Crawford County, Illinois close as water backs up\nMinnow Slough.  High water affects campground at Leaverton Park in\nPalestine. Water level is at the top of most\nmakeshift levees.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:00 PM EDT Wednesday /8:00 PM CDT Wednesday/ the stage\nwas 17.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 9:00 PM EDT Wednesday /8:00 PM CDT Wednesday/ was\n18.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon and continue falling and remain\nbelow flood stage.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued Thursday afternoon by around 100\nPM EDT /noon CDT/.",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:38PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nNavasota River near Normangee affecting Madison, Brazos and\nGrimes Counties.\n\nFor the Navasota River...including Normangee...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.\n\n* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding begins as water\nescapes the main channel and inundates the floodplain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 15.5 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:00 PM CDT Wednesday was 16.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 8.3 feet by\nMonday evening.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n15.4 feet on 04/30/1997.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "senderName": "NWS Little Rock AR",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:30PM CDT until June 29 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...\n\nCache River Near Patterson affecting Woodruff and Jackson\nCounties.\n\nFor the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Low swampy timberland along the river\nbegins to flood. Flood gates should be closed and equipment moved\nout of the low grounds along the river and tributaries.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 9.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nSunday morning and continue falling to 8.8 feet Monday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall\nforecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of\nflooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall\nforecasts.\n\nObserved and forecasted stage data plots are available on our\nAdvanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...\nwww.weather.gov/lzk\n\nUnder the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday evening at 830 PM CDT.",

            "description": "* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 kt, except north winds in Maalaea\nBay.\n\n* WHERE...Kauai Northwest Waters, Kauai Leeward Waters, Kauai\nChannel, Oahu Leeward Waters, Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel,\nAlenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters and Big Island\nSoutheast Waters.\n\n* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.",

            "senderName": "NWS Norman OK",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:10PM CDT until June 25 at 5:09PM CDT by NWS Norman OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nClear Boggy Creek near Caney affecting Atoka County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Clear Boggy Creek near Caney.\n\n* WHEN...Until tomorrow afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 29.0 feet, Creek levels rise to three feet higher\nthan flood stage in western Atoka County and the northeastern edge\nof Bryan County. High stages on small feeder streams result in\neven greater depths to mainstem bottomlands near their points of\nentry into Clear Boggy Creek. Croplands... pastures... and some\nsecondary rural roads are flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 28.6 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 26.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The Clear Boggy Creek is expected to fall below\nflood stage late tomorrow morning and continue falling.\n- Flood stage is 26.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:09PM EDT until June 27 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nGeorgia...\n\nSatilla River At Waycross affecting Ware and Pierce Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...\n\nSatilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.\n\nAdditional information is available at\nhttps://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Satilla River at Waycross.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Flooding of agriculture and timberlands\nbegins. On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat Ramp is\nflooded. On the Pierce/Brantley county line at the State Road 121\nBridge the boat ramp and dirt access roads are flooded.\nAt 17.0 feet, On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat\nRamp parking lot and access road is flooded and Simmons Trail is\nflooded cutting off one residence. On the Pierce County side, the\nOkefenokee Country Club Course Holes 14 through 16 begin to flood.\nAt 18.0 feet, On the Pierce County side, the Okefenokee Country\nClub Golf Course is generally closed. Riverwoods Drive low lying\nproperties begin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 17.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nFriday evening and continue falling to 15.1 feet Saturday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:07PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPascagoula River At Graham Ferry affecting Jackson County.\n\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Graham Ferry...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pascagoula River at Graham Ferry.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, River property at Cumbest Bluff will be cut\noff by high water and some river roads will be impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 16.9 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 16.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.5 feet\nearly Friday morning. The river is expected to fall below flood\nstage early Monday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.5\nfeet on 09/05/2012.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",
