            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 8:02PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, south central, and\nsoutheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Barton, Ellsworth, Lincoln, Marion, McPherson, Rice,\nRussell and Saline. In east central Kansas, Chase. In south\ncentral Kansas, Butler, Cowley, Harper, Harvey, Kingman, Reno,\nSedgwick and Sumner. In southeast Kansas, Allen, Chautauqua, Elk,\nGreenwood, Labette, Montgomery, Neosho, Wilson and Woodson.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 AM CDT Thursday through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Several rounds of thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall are\nexpected from late tonight through early Friday morning.\nWhile not everyone will see flooding from rainfall, it\nappears likely that several locations will receive enough\nrainfall to cause flooding concerns.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "FFAICT"
              ],

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nLittle Wabash River below Clay City affecting Richland and Clay\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Little Wabash River below Clay City.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.7 feet, Mayflower Road...just north of U.S. Route\n50...begins to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 20.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 6:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 21.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 20.2 feet Monday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:00PM CDT until June 29 at 5:30PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nEmbarras River at Lawrenceville affecting Lawrence County.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Embarras River at Lawrenceville.\n\n* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 33.0 feet, Kelly's Lake Lane, 1160N, is inundated.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 32.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 32.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 32.2\nfeet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below\nflood stage late Monday morning.\n- Flood stage is 30.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:59PM CDT until June 26 at 5:30AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nKansas...\n\nCow Creek near Hutchinson affecting Reno and Rice Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nArkansas River at Arkansas City affecting Cowley County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cow Creek near Hutchinson.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, The low water crossing on Wilson Rd\nbetween 69th Ave to 82nd Ave floods. Expect water depth near 4\ninches to a width of 5 feet.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 9.7 feet and is\ncresting.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.9\nfeet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below\nflood stage tomorrow afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 9.5 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 800 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:56PM CDT until June 28 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Alabama...\nFlorida...\n\nEscambia River Near Century affecting Escambia and Santa Rosa\nCounties.\n\nFor the Escambia River...including Century...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Escambia River near Century.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.0 feet, low lying pastures will flood. Cattle\nshould be moved to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 18.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early\nSunday morning and continue falling to 15.7 feet Monday evening.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates occur.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:55PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near Glenmora.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, When the river is falling and the gauge\nreading is forecast to be near 12 feet, flooding of forested areas\nnear the river will occur.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 13.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Wednesday was 13.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 12.5 feet Monday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:55PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near White Oak Park.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water over lowest portions of Goos Ferry\nRoad. Cars should be moved to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:35 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 3.4 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:35 PM CDT Wednesday was 4.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.4\nfeet just after midnight tonight.\n- Flood stage is 2.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:48PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nChickasawhay At Leakesville affecting Greene and George Counties.\n\nFor the Chickasawhay River...including Waynesboro, Leakesville...\nMinor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Chickasawhay at Leakesville.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, flooding at the highway bridge begins.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 26.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 23.2 feet Monday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates occur.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPascagoula At Merrill affecting Jackson, Greene and George\nCounties.\n\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Merrill...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pascagoula at Merrill.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, streets of Merrill will become flooded.             "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 24 at 7:46PM CDT until June 28 at 11:01PM CDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSappa Creek At Oberlin 1sw affecting Decatur County.\n\nFor the Sappa Creek...including Norcatur 15ne, Oberlin 1sw...\nelevated river levels are forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Sappa Creek at Oberlin 1sw.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon to late Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Water spreads over agricultural fields and\nlow lying areas with actual water depth in creek at about 6 feet.\nAt 15.0 feet, Moderate flooding will occur in nearby agricultural\nfields and low lying areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 10.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river may rise above flood stage tomorrow\nafternoon to a crest of 15.4 feet early Friday afternoon. It\nwill then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.\n- Action stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,\ntelevision, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.\n\nIf you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding\nor the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:42PM CDT until June 28 at 3:24PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Monticello affecting Lawrence County.\n\nPearl River Near Rockport affecting Simpson and Copiah Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Rockport.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 30.0 feet, Water begins to back up into higher\nagricultural and pasture lands, mainly on the Simpson County side\nof the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 28.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.5\nfeet tomorrow morning.\n- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.             "senderName": "NWS New Orleans LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:39PM CDT until July 3 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River County and\nWashington Parish.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting St. Tammany Parish and\nHancock and Pearl River Counties.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Bogalusa.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Woodlands and crop acreage along the river\nwill be flooded. The Bogue Chitto Wildlife Management area will be\ninundated with water in recreational camps and over access roads.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 19.3 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:15 PM CDT Wednesday was 19.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.0 feet\nearly Sunday afternoon. The river is expected to fall below flood\nstage Friday, July 03.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.0\nfeet on 02/14/2021.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River County and\nWashington Parish.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting St. Tammany Parish and\nHancock and Pearl River Counties.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Pearl River.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.5 feet, Secondary roads to the river and throughout\nHoney Island Swamp are inundated.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:37PM CDT until June 28 at 1:36AM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nBig Black River Near Bentonia affecting Yazoo and Madison\nCounties.\n\nBig Black River Near Bovina affecting Warren and Hinds Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Big Black River near Bovina.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, Several access roads along and near the\nriver are under water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 27.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nearly tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 31.0 feet Friday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.             "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Jackson MS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 7:37PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nBig Black River Near Bentonia affecting Yazoo and Madison\nCounties.\n\nBig Black River Near Bovina affecting Warren and Hinds Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Big Black River near Bentonia.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Friday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Low lying woodland areas along the river\nbegins to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 22.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 22.7\nfeet just after midnight tonight.\n- Flood stage is 22.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.water.noaa.gov/wfo/jan\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1030 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 7:12PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Kansas, including the following areas, Johnson\nKS, Leavenworth, Linn KS, Miami and Wyandotte and Missouri,\nincluding the following areas, Bates, Cass, Clay, Cooper, Henry,\nHoward, Jackson, Johnson MO, Lafayette, Pettis, Platte and Saline.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- A very moist airmass in place will bring the potential for high\nrainfall rates and flooding with any thunderstorms.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "description": "* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 424 Southeastern Humboldt\nCounty and northern Lander County, Fire Weather Zone 425 White\nPine and Northeast Nye Counties, Fire Weather Zone 426\nNorthern Nye County-Mojave, Fire Weather Zone 427 Central\nNevada- Toiyabe, Fire Weather Zone 438 W Elko County, N Eureka\nand Lander Counties N of I80, Fire Weather Zone 469 Central\nElko County and Fire Weather Zone 470 Eastern Elko County.\n\n* WIND...Sustained west winds 15 to 25 mph, with gusts 30 to 40\nmph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...Minimum relative humidity values as low as 7\npercent.\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",

            "senderName": "NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 6:04PM CDT until June 25 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of central Louisiana, including the following\nparishes, Avoyelles, Evangeline and St. Landry.\n\n* WHEN...Until 600 PM CDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads\nremain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to\nexcess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow\nmoving or standing water. It will take several hours for all the\nwater from these storms to work through local drainage systems in\nurban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 603 PM CDT, gauge reports indicated runoff and standing\nwater from previous excessive rainfall.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nMelville, Palmetto, Morrow, Bayou Current, Port Barre,\nLebeau, Big Cane, Goudeau, Dupont and Whiteville.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nKeep children away from storm drains, culverts, creeks and streams.\nWater levels can rise rapidly and sweep children away.\n\nStay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become\nunstable and unsafe.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "event": "Air Quality Alert",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 24 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",

            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 3:04PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "Multiple days of heavy rainfall has led to saturated soil across\nmuch of the Tri-State area. Additional rainfall is expected tonight\nthrough Thursday morning and could lead to flash flooding.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Kit\nCarson and Yuma, Kansas, including the following areas, Cheyenne\nKS, Decatur, Gove, Graham, Greeley, Logan, Norton, Rawlins,\nSheridan, Sherman, Thomas, Wallace and Wichita, and southwest\nNebraska, including the following areas, Dundy, Hitchcock and Red\nWillow.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in additional flooding of\nrivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone\nlocations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and\nflooding of creeks and rivers are possible. Area creeks and\nstreams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tucson AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 1:24PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with afternoon temperatures of\n106 to 109 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...Southeast Pinal County, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River\nValley, and Upper San Pedro River Valley (mainly north of Benson).\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 1:19PM MST until June 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a Fire Weather\nWatch for strong and gusty winds, low relative humidity, and high\nto very high fire danger, which is in effect from Saturday\nmorning through Sunday evening.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 150, 151, 152, 153 and 154.\n\n* TIMING...From 10 AM MST Saturday through 8 PM MST Sunday.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 to 40 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...8 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop or are ongoing will have the\npotential to spread rapidly.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur.             "description": "The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Red Flag\nWarning, which is in effect until midnight AKDT tonight.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Upper Kobuk Valleys and Lower Koyukuk Valley.\n\n* TIMING...Until midnight AKDT tonight.\n\n* WINDS...Northwest 8 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...As low as 20 to 25 percent.\n\n* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Lows in the lower 50s.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are developing\nWednesday due to a combination of hot temperatures, low relative\nhumidity, gusty winds from the west, and dry fuels.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...RH recovery tonight will likely reach above 70\npercent for low lying areas in valleys and along rivers.\nHot and dry conditions continue Thursday with sustained wind\nspeeds likely less than 15 mph.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that conditions are occurring or will\noccur which could lead to the development of large and dangerous\nfires.             "senderName": "NWS San Diego CA",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 24 at 12:40PM PDT until June 25 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures up to 110 San\nDiego County Deserts.\n\n* WHERE...San Diego County Deserts.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Thursday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nDo not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car\ninteriors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Dodge City KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 2:17PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS",
            "description": "The active wet pattern continues across southwest Kansas, with\nanother thunderstorm complex expected late Wednesday night through\nThursday. Topsoils have become saturated, with any additional\nrainfall leading to runoff concerns.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, south central, southwest, and west\ncentral Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Ellis and Rush. In south central Kansas, Barber, Comanche,\nEdwards, Kiowa, Pawnee, Pratt and Stafford. In southwest Kansas,\nClark, Finney, Ford, Grant, Gray, Hamilton, Haskell, Hodgeman,\nKearny, Meade, Morton, Seward, Stanton and Stevens. In west\ncentral Kansas, Lane, Ness, Scott and Trego.\n\n* WHEN...From 1 AM CDT  /midnight MDT/ Thursday through late\nThursday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Area creeks\nand streams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 1-2 inches are expected to be\ncommon Thursday.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "FFADDC"
              ],

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 12:04PM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Reno has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for gusty winds and low humidity, which is in effect from\n11 AM Friday to 11 PM PDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch has\nbeen upgraded to a Red Flag Warning.\n\n* CHANGES...Fire Weather Watch upgraded to a Red Flag Warning.\n\n* Affected Area...Fire Weather Zone 420 Northern Sierra Front\nincluding Carson City, Douglas, Storey, Southern Washoe,\nWestern Lyon, and Far Southern Lassen Counties.\n\n* Winds...West 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.\n\n* Humidity...Afternoon minimums 12 to 20 percent.\n\n* Duration...2 to 4 hours Friday with 3 to 8 hours Saturday.\nWhile humidity will recover Friday night, winds will stay breezy\non midslopes and ridges.\n\n* Impacts...The combination of gusty winds and low humidity can\ncause fire to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first\nresponders can contain them, especially from any recent\nlightning holdovers.",
            "instruction": "Avoid outdoor activities that can cause a spark near dry\nvegetation, such as yard work, target shooting, or campfires.\nFollow local fire restrictions. Check weather.gov/reno for\nupdates and livingwithfire.info for preparedness tips.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Watch issued June 24 at 12:53PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive\nrainfall are possible over the South Fork Burn Scar Area.\n\n* WHERE...The South Fork Burn Scar Area in the northern Nebraska\npanhandle and downstream areas along Soldier Creek and the White\nRiver, including Fort Robinson and Crawford.\n\n* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Localized thunderstorm heavy rainfall over the South\nFork Burn Scar Area is possible. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms\nare expected in the area through Thursday evening. Residents near\nthe South Fork Burn Scar Area should prepare for potential\nflooding impacts. Be sure to stay up to date with information from\nlocal authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of\nlow-lying areas, urbanized street flooding, and debris flows in\nand near recent wildfire burn scars.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting\nlocally heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to\nflash flooding and debris flows.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 24 at 11:33AM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV",
            "description": "...FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FOR MUCH OF THE REGION\nFRIDAY AND SATURDAY DUE TO GUSTY WINDS AND LOW HUMIDITIES...\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...In Arizona...Fire weather zone 101 and 102. In\nCalifornia...Fire weather zones 227 and 229. In Nevada... Fire\nweather zones 460, 461, 462, 463, 464, 465, and 466.\n\n* TIMING...From Friday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* WIND...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 50 mph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...5 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "senderName": "NWS Spokane WA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 11:31AM PDT until June 27 at 11:19PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nWashington...\n\nStehekin River at Stehekin affecting Chelan County.\n\nFor the Stehekin River...including Stehekin...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Stehekin River at Stehekin.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.5 feet, Water inundates some properties and\novertops the temporary corduroy bridge. Company Creek Road\ninundated at northern end. Battalion Creek culverts are beginning\nto be overtopped. Water begins damaging Wood Road.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:30 AM PDT Wednesday the stage was 20.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 19.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 10:30 AM PDT Wednesday was 20.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will fluctuate between 20.6 and 20.9\nfeet through Thursday. It will fall begin falling, and\ndropping flood stage this weekend.\n- Flood stage is 20.5 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 1215 PM PDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 24 at 12:17PM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID",
            "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THURSDAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT\nTHURSDAY NIGHT FOR SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE\n413...\n\nThe National Weather Service in Pocatello has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for scattered thunderstorms, which is in effect from 9 AM\nThursday to midnight MDT Thursday night.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 413 Caribou Range/Caribou NF.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected.\nLightning may generate new fire starts. Any new fire starts or\nexisting fires may spread rapidly\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...25 to 35 percent coverage.\n\n* OUTFLOW WINDS...35 to 55 mph.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria\nfor Southeastern Idaho:\n\n- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at\nleast 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.\n\n- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall\ncriteria.\n\n- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National\nWeather Service and area fire management agencies.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "senderName": "NWS Topeka KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 24 at 11:53AM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Topeka KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, and\nnortheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Dickinson. In east central Kansas, Anderson, Coffey,\nDouglas, Franklin, Geary, Lyon, Morris, Osage, Shawnee and\nWabaunsee. In north central Kansas, Ottawa. In northeast Kansas,\nJefferson.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Forecast rainfall amounts of one to three inches Thursday and\nThursday night could lead to scattered flooding, mainly of\narea creeks, streams and rivers.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 10:16AM CDT until June 27 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Paducah KY has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Indiana...Illinois...\n\nWabash River at New Harmony.\n\n.Recent heavy rainfall is continuing to cause rises on the Wabash\nRiver.  At New Harmony, the river will climb above flood stage this\nevening, cresting around a half foot above flood stage Friday.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to late Saturday evening.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 14.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate this evening to a crest of 15.5 feet early Friday\nmorning. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 24 at 9:10AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Rio Blanco, Garfield, Eagle, Pitkin, Mesa, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray, Dolores, San Juan,\nMontezuma, La Plata, Hinsdale, Mineral and Saguache Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Meeker, Rangely,\nGlenwood Springs, Eagle, Vail, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Telluride, Ouray, Dove Creek,\nSilverton, Cortez, Durango, Hermosa, Honeyville, Rockwood, Lake\nCity, Creede and Saguache.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Wednesday June 24 to 900 AM Thursday June 25\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",

            "response": "Monitor",

            "senderName": "NWS Chicago IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 8:52AM CDT until June 27 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at La Salle affecting Putnam, Bureau and La Salle\nCounties.\n\nFor the Illinois River (Upper)...including La Salle...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River from Starved Rock Lock and Dam downstream\nto confluence with Big Bureau Creek, including the La Salle gauge.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Lower parking lot at Starved Rock State\nPark is inundated east of La Salle. High water levels begin to\nimpact shipping interests along the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 22.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nSaturday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or\nmay already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the\nwarned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and\nproperty.\n\nThese forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as\nforecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the\nrainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may\ncause changes to these river forecasts.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by late tonight.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 24 at 9:09AM EDT until June 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nFlorida...\n\nChoctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20) affecting Washington and\nWalton Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Choctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20).\n\n* WHEN...From this morning to early Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Big Cedar, Cowford, and Choctawhatchee\nRiver Roads begin to flood in Walton County. Flood waters impact\nstorage areas underneath homes on the west banks of the\nChoctawhatchee River. Low areas along Strickland Road in\nWashington County become subject to flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was estimated to be around\n14.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate this morning to a crest of 14.8 feet early tomorrow\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Sunday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n14.8 feet on 03/11/1934.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "* WHAT...Critical fire weather conditions. Southwest winds 20 to 30\nmph with gusts 40 to 50 mph and relative humidity 8 to 16 percent\nexpected each afternoon.\n\n* WHERE...All of northern Arizona.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning through Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rapid spread and growth of any new or existing fires.\nFires will have the potential to exhibit extreme fire behavior.\nElevated potential for new fire starts. Winds may damage power\nlines, resulting in new fire starts.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are\npossible. These conditions could promote the rapid spread and growth\nof wildfires, which could become life-threatening. For forecast\nupdates, go to weather.gov/flagstaff.\n\nIf you have not packed your go kit yet, now is the time to do so.\nThis includes items like important documents and essentials you\ncannot live without. Fill your vehicle's fuel tank. Visit\nready.gov/kit for more information.\n\nObey all fire restrictions. To view a map of current fire\nrestrictions, go to wildlandfire.az.gov/fire-restrictions.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of\nthis Fire Weather Watch.",
